title: Brush Paint Fills mode wrongly excludes empty areas — Flash 8 paints fills AND empty areas, leaving only lines unaffected
description:
VERIFIED vs Flash 8 documentation; our implementation (and docs/04 + tests, which codified the wrong semantics) diverges.

FLASH 8 GROUND TRUTH (Using Flash, Brush tool modifiers):
- Paint Normal: paints over lines and fills on the same layer.
- Paint Fills: paints fills AND EMPTY AREAS, leaving lines unaffected.
- Paint Behind: paints only blank areas, leaving lines and fills unaffected.
The distinguishing feature of Paint Fills vs Normal is that it does not obliterate LINES — not that it refuses to paint empty canvas.

BUG: engine/planar/brushpaint.ts:156-166 ('fills' case) keeps only sub-faces over an EXISTING fill (returns null over empty canvas: 'if (existingStage.length === 0) return null'), so brushing across a fill onto the background clips the stroke at the fill boundary and a Paint Fills stroke on empty canvas paints nothing. In real Flash 8 that stroke paints everywhere except it leaves stroke/line pixels intact. brush-paintmode.test.ts:77-95 and docs/04-toolbox.md:84-92 assert the incorrect behavior and must be updated with the code.

SUGGESTED FIX: 'fills' keep-predicate accepts BOTH filled faces and empty/background faces (i.e., geometrically like 'normal'), with the mode's real distinction being stroke preservation: the ribbon must not consume/replace covered line segments (see task 1430 — under today's fold, lines are never consumed anyway, so once 1430 lands 'fills' = normal-clip + preserve-lines; until then 'fills' can simply not clip). Keep 'behind' as-is (empty-only is correct).

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests — (a) Paint Fills over empty canvas commits the full ribbon; (b) Paint Fills across a fill + background paints both sides; (c) Paint Fills over a fill crossed by a line leaves the line's covered segments intact (asserts jointly with 1430); docs/04 updated to the authentic mode table.

Related: 1421 (introduced the modes), 1430 (fill-over-line consumption). Found by brush/eraser Flash-8 fidelity audit.
